name: Custom Vinyl Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Vinyl Stickers, Any Shape | The Die Cut Stickers
seoDescription: Custom vinyl stickers on white, clear, holographic or metallic vinyl. Gloss, matte or spot UV, any shape from 0.5 inch to 24 x 36 inches, free US shipping.
tagline: Weather-rated vinyl, printed in full color and cut square, round, kiss cut or to your outline.
quickAnswer: Custom vinyl stickers are printed on a flexible PVC film with a permanent or removable adhesive, then finished with gloss, matte or spot UV and an optional laminate. They suit anyone who needs a sticker that survives rain, sun and handling: product labels, car and window graphics, laptop decals, fleet lettering. From $0.30 per sticker, 100-piece minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.

sections.h2: What this vinyl page covers, and when you want the die cut page instead
sections.html:
Vinyl is the material we print more of than anything else, and this page is the general vinyl page: white vinyl, clear vinyl, holographic and metallic films, in every cut style we run. Squares, circles and rounded rectangles cut to size, kiss cut sheets where the backing stays whole, roll stickers for a label applicator, and full contour cuts around the artwork. If you know you want a logo cut exactly to its outline with a thin border, the die cut vinyl sticker page is set up for that job specifically, with its own pricing notes on complex outlines. Come here when the question is still open: which vinyl, which finish, which adhesive, which size.

The practical difference between vinyl and the paper stocks is water. A paper label on a cold bottle wrinkles inside an hour. Vinyl stays flat, the ink stays put under the laminate, and the adhesive keeps gripping through condensation, dish soap and a car wash.

sections.h2: Surfaces vinyl grips well, and the few it struggles with
sections.html:
The adhesive we use on vinyl is a pressure-sensitive acrylic. It bonds to smooth, clean, non-porous surfaces almost immediately and reaches full strength in about 24 hours. A quick wipe with isopropyl alcohol before application removes the skin oils and dust that cause the corners to lift later.

  • Glass and clear acrylic: windows, jars, display cases, phone cases.
  • Painted metal and clear-coated car panels, with no issue at the automatic car wash once cured.
  • Hard plastics such as HDPE bottles, polycarbonate laptops, PET tumblers and tool cases.
  • Sealed or laminated wood, including finished furniture and cabinet doors.
  • Coated cardboard and rigid boxes, where the sticker doubles as a seal.

Where vinyl disappoints: raw brick, unsealed concrete, textured stucco and low-energy plastics like polypropylene storage bins. The adhesive has nothing flat to hold onto. For those surfaces, a bigger sticker does not help; you need a different adhesive, and we will say so before you order rather than after.

sections.h2: Gloss, matte, spot UV or laminate: which finish fits the job
sections.html:
Finish changes how the sticker looks under light and how long the print survives. Laminate is a second clear film pressed over the print; it adds scratch protection and is what stretches outdoor life toward the top of the range.

FinishLookBest forOutdoor life (laminated)
GlossShiny, deep color, shows fingerprintsProduct labels, bumper stickers, bright logos3 to 5 years
MatteNo glare, soft color, easy to readPackaging, laptop decals, text-heavy designs3 to 5 years
Spot UVGloss highlights on a matte basePremium labels, logo marks you want to raise2 to 3 years
Unlaminated glossShiny, slightly less scratch resistantIndoor use, short promotions, giveaways1 to 2 years

If you cannot decide between the two main finishes, send us the artwork. Dark backgrounds with small white type read better in matte; photos and saturated brand colors usually look richer in gloss.

sections.h2: Vinyl stickers for cars, fleet lettering and storefront glass
sections.html:
A lot of vinyl orders are for vehicles. Bumper stickers at 3 x 11.5 inches, rear-window logos at 6 to 10 inches wide, door lettering for a plumbing van at 18 inches or more. We print all of these on the same outdoor-grade vinyl with a laminate as standard for vehicle use, because an unlaminated print on a hood takes a beating from UV and gravel.

Vinyl lettering is a different product from a printed sticker. With lettering, each letter is cut separately and delivered on transfer tape, so there is no background at all. With a printed vinyl sticker, the whole shape is one piece with a white or clear background, which is faster to apply and cheaper per unit. We make both, and the choice usually comes down to how big the words are and how many vehicles you are doing. Our full catalog of custom stickers on the Die Cut Stickers home page lists the vehicle and window options side by side.

sections.h2: How a wholesale vinyl sticker order moves from file to FedEx
sections.html:
Wholesale means the same product at a lower unit price because the setup is shared across more pieces. At 100 stickers you pay the most per piece; at 1,000 and 5,000 the price per sticker drops sharply because the press time barely changes.

  1. Send the artwork as PDF, AI, EPS, SVG, or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG, with the finished size in inches and the quantity.
  2. Tell us the surface it goes on and indoors or out. That decides adhesive and laminate.
  3. We email a digital proof within one business day, usually with the cut line drawn in so you can see the border.
  4. Approve the proof or ask for changes. Design help is free and there is no limit on rounds.
  5. Production takes 5 to 7 business days, then FedEx ground delivers free anywhere in the United States, typically 8 to 10 business days from approval.

Rush production is available when you ask at the quote stage, not after the proof is approved.

sections.h2: When plain white vinyl is the wrong pick
sections.html:
White vinyl is opaque, so any area you leave unprinted shows white. On a clear bottle or a glass door that white box around the logo looks cheap. Clear vinyl fixes it, with a white ink layer printed under the colors so they stay solid. For packaging that has to catch the eye on a shelf, our custom holographic stickers use the same adhesive and finishes on a rainbow film, and we can print them on the same order so the shipment arrives together.

The other trade-off is removability. Permanent adhesive is the right call for labels and vehicles. Removable adhesive is the right call for laptops, seasonal promotions and anything on a rented wall, because it peels clean within a year or so. Ask for it by name; we default to permanent.

faqs.a: Yes. The vinyl film itself does not absorb water, and the acrylic adhesive keeps its grip when wet. Add a laminate and the printed ink is sealed too, so the sticker holds up on water bottles, coolers, boats and cars through rain and car washes.

faqs.q: How many custom vinyl stickers do I have to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers per design. That floor covers the setup for a single artwork. If you need several designs, each one counts as its own 100-piece run, though we can gang similar sizes on one sheet to keep the unit price lower.

faqs.q: What is the price difference between 100 and 1,000 vinyl stickers?
faqs.a: Pricing starts at $0.30 per sticker and drops as quantity rises, because the press setup is the same for 100 or 1,000 pieces. A 3-inch die cut at 1,000 pieces usually costs well under half the per-sticker price of the same job at 100.

faqs.q: Can I order custom vinyl stickers wholesale for resale?
faqs.a: Yes. Many of our customers are print brokers, promotional product sellers and Etsy shops who resell. Wholesale runs ship in plain cartons with no branding of ours, and we can split one order into separate counts per design on request.

faqs.q: Will custom vinyl stickers for cars survive a car wash?
faqs.a: A laminated vinyl sticker on a clean, cured surface goes through automatic and pressure car washes without lifting. Apply it at least 24 hours before the first wash, and keep the pressure wand a foot or more from the sticker edge.

faqs.q: Do vinyl stickers damage car paint when removed?
faqs.a: On factory clear coat, no. Warm the sticker with a hair dryer, peel slowly at a low angle, and wipe any adhesive trace with a citrus-based remover. Repainted panels with a thin or uncured clear coat are the exception, so test on a hidden spot first.

faqs.q: Is vinyl lettering the same as a custom vinyl sticker?
faqs.a: No. Vinyl lettering is cut from solid colored film with each letter separate on transfer tape, and there is no background. A custom vinyl sticker is printed in full color as one piece. Lettering reads cleaner on glass; printed stickers handle gradients, photos and small type.

faqs.q: Which vinyl thickness should I pick for my stickers?
faqs.a: Three mil is the standard for labels and indoor decals and is easiest to wrap around curves. Four mil is our usual pick for vehicles and outdoor signs. Five mil is stiffer, handy for large graphics that get applied by hand without a squeegee.

faqs.q: Can the same vinyl sticker order include different sizes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as each size meets the 100-piece minimum. We lay each size out as its own run, so a 2-inch and a 4-inch version of the same logo are quoted separately, then packed and shipped together in one FedEx box.

faqs.q: How do I apply a large vinyl sticker without bubbles?
faqs.a: Clean the surface with isopropyl alcohol, then peel back only an inch of liner, stick that edge down and squeegee outward in strokes, peeling the liner as you go. For anything over 12 inches, a light mist of soapy water lets you slide it into place first.

faqs.q: Does white vinyl show a white border around my logo?
faqs.a: Only where you leave it. A die cut sticker gets a thin white border, usually 1/16 to 1/8 inch, so the cut never clips the artwork. If you want no visible edge on a dark or glass surface, we switch the base to clear vinyl and print white ink behind the colors.

faqs.q: What file do you need for a custom vinyl sticker proof?
faqs.a: Vector files (PDF, AI, EPS or SVG) give the cleanest edges at any size. If you only have a PNG or JPG, make it 300 dpi at the finished size. Send it with the size in inches and we return a proof with the cut line drawn in.
